statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39836 (GO-2026-4971): on Windows, net.Dial and net.LookupPort in the Go standard library panic when given input that contains a NUL byte. It is fixed in Go 1.25.10 and 1.26.3: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-4971, https://go.dev/issue/79006, https://go.dev/cl/775320, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/3baf3eec3b2247bbfbdeac4193c88baa7acc0842 (in go1.26.3, not go1.26.2), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/qcCIEXso47M . We downloaded all 36 alertmanager-dev builds listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), for x86_64 and aarch64, and checked each download against the index checksum. Each package holds two regular files and no symbolic links: /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, Go programs built with GOOS=linux, CGO_ENABLED=0 and -ldflags -s -w. We read each program's function table from the Go line table, which works on these stripped binaries and finds runtime.main in every program, and searched each program's bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go toolchain in the build information, the same for both programs and both architectures, is: 0.31.1-r0 with Go 1.25.7; 0.31.1-r1 to 0.31.1-r4 with Go 1.26.1; 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r0 with Go 1.26.2; 0.32.1-r1 to 0.32.1-r2 with Go 1.26.3; 0.32.1-r3 to 0.33.1-r0 with Go 1.26.4; 0.33.1-r1 to 0.33.1-r3 with Go 1.26.5; 0.33.1-r5 to 0.34.0-r0 with Go 1.26.6; 0.34.0-r1 with Go 1.26.7; 0.34.0-r2 to 0.34.1-r1 with Go 1.26.8; 0.34.1-r2 to 0.34.1-r3 with Go 1.26.9; 0.34.1-r4 to 0.35.0-r0 with Go 1.26.10; 0.35.0-r1 to 0.35.0-r2 with Go 1.26.11. The Go vulnerability database entry has no operating-system restriction, and the function tables of both programs do contain several of its listed net functions (Dial, Dialer.DialContext, Resolver.LookupPort and others) in every build. The bug, however, is only in Windows code: the fix replaces calls to syscall.StringToUTF16Ptr, which panics on a NUL byte, with syscall.UTF16PtrFromString, which returns an error, and apart from a one-line test case in src/net/lookup_test.go it changes only src/net/lookup_windows.go and src/syscall/syscall_windows.go, which the _windows file name limits to Windows builds, and key.go and value.go of internal/syscall/windows/registry, which carry the //go:build windows constraint. Go compiles none of those files for GOOS=linux. In no build does either program's function table contain an internal/syscall/windows function or a UTF16 conversion function, and the byte search of every program finds no internal/syscall/windows. name. As a check, a test program built with Go 1.26.2 whose function table contains net Dialer.DialContext and Resolver.LookupPort has internal/syscall/windows functions and the syscall functions StringToUTF16Ptr and UTF16FromString in its function table when built for windows/amd64, and none of them, nor any internal/syscall/windows. bytes, when built for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any build of this package.
